title: What It Actually Looks Like to Be Hard on Yourself and Gentle with Everyone Else
caption:
He's twenty minutes late again and you feel the irritation before he even sits down. You skipped your own discipline twice this week and never gave yourself a second thought.

Most guys have that backwards. Sharp with everyone else's sin, soft on their own. A godly man runs it the other way: hardest on himself, gentlest with everyone else.

That means confession comes before correction. It means giving him the same benefit of the doubt you'd want on the week you dropped the ball.

"Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother's eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye?" (Matthew 7:3)

Hard on the sin in the mirror. Gentle with the man across the table.

Save this for the next time you're about to say something about him before you've said anything to yourself.

theme: He's hard on himself, gentle with others.
